options: How fast work is done — energy per second
How much total work was done
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, work per second — the tempo of energy.
questions.misconception: Power is often confused with total work; rate is the key difference.

questions.prompt: You do 600 J of work in 2 seconds. What is your power?
questions.misconception: Multiplying (1200) or misplacing which way to divide (150) are the classic slips.

questions.prompt: Two machines do the same work; machine A finishes in 1 second, machine B in 4 seconds. Which has higher power?
questions.explanation: Same work in less time means higher power — A divides by 1, B by 4.
questions.misconception: It is tempting to call them equal because the work matches; the rate, not the total, sets power.

questions.explanation: The watt is joules divided by seconds; a 60 W bulb spends 60 J each second.
questions.misconception: Mixing the watt with force-time combinations misses the joules-per-second definition.

questions.prompt: Two runners, same time: runner A transfers 100 J, runner B transfers 200 J. Who has more power?
questions.explanation: Same time with more work means higher power — power = work ÷ time, and B's numerator is bigger.
questions.misconception: Assuming equality because the time matched; the extra energy also counts.
